chunks: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, commanded Ibrahim to build the Kaaba and to raise its foundations and show the people their rituals. So Ibrahim and Ismail built the House every day, course by course, until they reached the place of the Black Stone.

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Then Mount Abu Qubays called out to Ibrahim (peace be upon him): 'There is a trust with me for you!' So it gave him the Stone, and he placed it in its place. Then Ibrahim (peace be upon him) called out among the people for the Hajj and said: 'O people! I am Ibrahim, the Friend of God! God commands you to perform the Hajj of this House, so perform its Hajj!' So those who would perform Hajj until the Day of Resurrection answered him, and the first to answer him were from the people of Yemen.

He said: And Ibrahim (peace be upon him) performed the Hajj — he himself, his family, and his children. So whoever claims that the one to be slaughtered was Ishaq — it would have been from this very place he was slaughtered.
And it is mentioned from Abu Basir that he heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) both claiming that it was Ishaq, while Zurara claimed that it was Ismail.

key_terms.أبو قبيس: Mount Abu Qubays — a mountain adjacent to Mecca, believed in Islamic tradition to have been a repository for the Black Stone
key_terms.الحجر الأسود: The Black Stone — a sacred stone embedded in the eastern corner of the Kaaba, said to have descended from Paradise
key_terms.الذبيح: The one to be slaughtered — the son whom Ibrahim (AS) was commanded to sacrifice; the identity (Ismail or Ishaq) is a matter of scholarly debate
key_terms.الكعبة: The Kaaba — the cubic structure at the center of al-Masjid al-Haram in Mecca, the holiest site in Islam
key_terms.خليل الله: Friend of God (Khalilullah) — a title of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), from Quran 4:125

ai.seo_question: What does al-Kafi narrate about Ibrahim and Ismail building the Kaaba and the Black Stone?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the divine command to Prophet Ibrahim (AS) to build the Kaaba and establish the rites of Hajj. The narrative includes the miraculous retrieval of the Black Stone from Mount Abu Qubays, Ibrahim's proclamation calling humanity to pilgrimage — a call that reverberates through all time — and his personal performance of Hajj. It concludes with a scholarly discussion among early Shia authorities about the identity of the 'Dhabih' (the one offered for sacrifice) — with Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq reportedly claiming it was Ishaq, while Zurara reported it was Ismail, reflecting an ongoing theological debate.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abduwayh Bin Aamir, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ahmad Bni Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Aban Bin usman, from Uqba Bin Basheer, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) having said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commanded Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> with the building of the House (Kaaba), and that he<sup>as</sup> should raise its foundations, and show the people their rituals (to be performed). Therefore, Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> and Ismail<sup>as</sup> built the House (Kaaba) every day, endeavouring, until they ended up to the place of the (Black) Stone’.

Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> called out on (Mount) Abu Qubays: ‘There is an entrustment with me<sup>as</sup> for you!’ So he<sup>as</sup> gave it the (Black) Stone, and he<sup>as</sup> placed it in its place. Then Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> called out among the people with the Hajj, so he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O you people! I<sup>as</sup> am Ibrahim<sup>as</sup>, the Friend of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Commands you all that you should be performing the Hajj of this House (Kaaba)! So perform its Hajj!’ So they answered, the ones who would be performing Hajj, up to the Day of Judgement, and the first one who answered him<sup>as</sup> were from the people of Al-Yemen’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And Ibrahim<sup>as</sup> performed Hajj, him<sup>as</sup> and his<sup>as</sup> wife and his children. So the one who claims that the slaughtered one, he was Is’haq, so it is from over here he was slaughtered’.

And it is mentioned from Abu Baseer that he heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> both claiming that it was Is’haq, and as for Zurara, so he claimes that it was Ismail<sup>as</sup>.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and al-Husayn ibn Muhammad have narrated from ‘ Abdawayh ibn ‘Amir and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Uqbah ibn Bashir who has said the following: “One of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said that Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, commanded Ibrahim to build al-Ka‘bah, to raise its foundations and show people how to perform the acts of their hajj. Ibrahim and Isma‘il built the House. They did it by doing a certain amount every day until they ended at the place where there is the Black Stone.

Abu Ja’far has said that abu Qubays (hill), then called Ibrahim saying, ‘There is something in trust for you with me.’ It gave the Black Stone to him and he placed it in its place. Ibrahim then called people for Hajj saying, ‘O people, I am Ibrahim, the friend of Allah, and Allah commands you to perform Hajj of this House so you must perform Hajj.’ Thus, all those who up to the Day of Judgment perform Hajj answered his call. The first one who answered his call was from Yemen.
He (the Imam) said, ‘Ibrahim, his family and children performed Hajj. Those who think that the person to be slaughtered was Ishaq they do so because of this.”’
It is said that abu Basir had heard this Hadith from abu Ja’far and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam. These two people think that Ishaq was the one but Zurarah thinks that he was Isma‘il.
